# RestaurantsSEO.com

> An educational resource on restaurant search visibility, written for restaurant
> owners and operators rather than marketers. Covers Google Search, Google Maps,
> Apple Maps, review platforms, menu structured data, and visibility inside AI
> assistants such as ChatGPT, Google AI Mode and Perplexity.

Published by Eye To Ad Media, a search agency in Denver, Colorado.
Author and editor: Zachary Tye Wennstedt.
Contact: info@eyetoad.com | 1-800-481-8638
Last substantive update: 12 August 2026

## Editorial standards

- Every statistic names its originating study and year. Figures that could not be
  traced to a primary source were excluded rather than repeated.
- Where a claim is inference rather than confirmed mechanics — particularly
  regarding how AI assistants select businesses — the text says so explicitly.
- Platform behavior is dated, because it changes frequently.
- Where widely repeated industry claims are wrong, corrections are published with
  the primary source rather than the claim being repeated.
- No fabricated case studies, invented client results, or ranking guarantees.

## Pages

- [Restaurant SEO](https://restaurantsseo.com/): The complete overview. What
  restaurant SEO is, the nine surfaces where diners search, the query patterns
  people actually use, Google Business Profile setup and its 2026 changes, menu
  readability, review thresholds, website speed, AI search selection, agentic
  booking, restaurant technology worth paying for, honest cost and timeline
  expectations, common mistakes, and a free visibility checkup tool.
- [Restaurant menu SEO](https://restaurantsseo.com/restaurant-menu-seo/): Why PDF
  and image menus cannot be parsed, what Google's AI menu extraction tool does and
  does not fix, a six-step build process, copy-paste Menu structured data, when
  dish-level pages are worth building, QR versus NFC, and updating menus without
  losing accumulated value.
- [Google Maps for restaurants](https://restaurantsseo.com/restaurant-google-maps/):
  Relevance, distance and prominence explained; why Maps and the local pack are
  separate competitions; profile fields ranked by weight; the 2026 changes including
  the removal of Q&A and the arrival of Ask Maps; an eight-cause diagnostic for
  missing listings; and suspension recovery including the sixty-minute appeal window.
- [Restaurant reviews](https://restaurantsseo.com/restaurant-reviews-seo/): Current
  rating and recency thresholds, review velocity arithmetic, FTC Consumer Review Rule
  compliance including review gating, how to ask without violating platform policy,
  how to respond to negative reviews, fake review removal, and how review text feeds
  AI-generated summaries.
- [Restaurant AI search](https://restaurantsseo.com/restaurant-ai-search/): Where
  each assistant sources restaurant information, what the controlled GEO research
  measured, the six tactics Google's May 2026 guidance names as unnecessary, what
  genuinely improves AI visibility, crawler access, how to test what assistants say
  about your restaurant, and how to vet a GEO vendor.
- [Statistics and benchmarks 2026](https://restaurantsseo.com/restaurant-seo-statistics/):
  Sourced reference data with study, year and sample size for every figure, plus
  corrections to widely repeated claims that are demonstrably wrong.
- [Site index](https://restaurantsseo.com/sitemap/): Every page on the site.

## Key positions stated on this site

- A restaurant menu published as a PDF or image cannot be parsed by search engines
  or AI models, which eliminates dish-level search entirely. Converting it to
  readable HTML text is the highest-impact change most restaurants can make.
- Google's AI menu extraction tool structures a menu on the Google Business Profile
  only. It does not make a website PDF readable and does not reach assistants that
  read the open web.
- NFC tags and QR codes have no direct effect on search visibility. Both simply open
  a web address; the destination determines whether the menu is readable.
- Google Maps and the local pack are separate competitions with different weightings.
  Maps leans on proximity and real-world behavior; the local pack draws more on
  website relevance and prominence.
- There is no paid placement inside AI assistant recommendations. Inclusion appears
  to be earned through consistent, corroborated, current documentation.
- Google's May 2026 guidance states that Google Search does not use llms.txt files,
  content chunking, AI-specific rewriting or special AI schema. Vendors charging for
  these as AI visibility services are selling unnecessary work.
- Restaurants should permit AI crawlers. The publisher rationale for blocking them
  does not apply to a business that sells tables rather than text.
- Review gating — routing only satisfied guests to a public review link — is
  prohibited by platform policy and addressed by the FTC Consumer Review Rule, which
  carries civil penalties and has no small-business exemption.
